source_batch.unit_label: BRBL::MOD_C::U10: Separate registration, public notice, enforcement entitlement and priority

facts.statement: Sections26B-C permit specified other-creditor/attachment filings with notifications and public-notice effect; non-secured-creditor filing confers noSARFAESI enforcement.26D registration condition;26E priority read subjectIBC qualification in primary.

payload.title: One filing can have several effects without changing creditor status
payload.core_explanation_md:
Section26B extends the described filing framework to other creditors and attachment orders through its applicable notification conditions. A creditor outside the defined secured-creditor class does not acquire ChapterIII enforcement powers merely by making such a filing. Section26C separately gives the stated public-notice effect from filing date and time and addresses later transactions, with its ordinary-course qualification.

Section26D makes the required Central Registry registration a condition for the secured creditor enforcement right. Section26E addresses priority after registration, with the statutory insolvency/bankruptcy qualification. Keep status, filing, notice, enforcement and priority as five distinct checks; none can be replaced by a single green registration flag.

self_check.prompt_text: Does an other-creditor filing by itself make its holder a SARFAESI secured creditor?
self_check.expected_takeaway: No. Filing does not override the creditor-status and enforcement provisions.

payload.stem_md: A creditor outside the defined secured-creditor class files particulars under the permitted other-creditor framework and claims ChapterIII powers solely on that basis. What is the error?

options.text_md: All other-creditor records must be deleted regardless of notification
options.explanation_md: The framework permits the stated filings subject to its conditions.

options.text_md: Filing is being confused with the separate statutory entitlement to enforce
options.explanation_md: Section26B preserves the distinction for creditors outside the defined class.

options.text_md: Public notice automatically cancels the debt
options.explanation_md: The filing gives notice effects, not discharge.

options.text_md: An attachment necessarily proves final payment
options.explanation_md: An attachment order is not proof of satisfaction.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Section26B preserves the distinction for creditors outside the defined class.

payload.stem_md: A priority memo invokes section26E but ignores pending insolvency proceedings. Which refinement is necessary?

options.text_md: Registration overrides the IBC without qualification
options.explanation_md: The provision contains an insolvency/bankruptcy qualification.

options.text_md: All registered securities become unsecured automatically
options.explanation_md: Pending proceedings do not justify that blanket conclusion.

options.text_md: A filing timestamp decides every insolvency distribution alone
options.explanation_md: The applicable insolvency framework must also be examined.

options.text_md: Read the priority claim with the statutory IBC qualification and proceeding facts
options.explanation_md: Priority cannot be asserted without its applicable legal context.

payload.correct_explanation_md: Priority cannot be asserted without its applicable legal context.
